scope: 64 districts; dated upazila directory snapshot; three verified mouzas. Nationwide upazila and mouza completeness is NOT established.
english_name_policy: Stored human transliterations of verified Bangla names; not claimed as official English spellings

sources.title: Bangladesh Gazette, 14 August 2014, Part VI, printed page 1485 (PDF page 11)
sources.evidence: Schedule explicitly identifies district Dhaka, upazila Savar, mouzas Bara Kakar and Birulia.

sources.title: Bangladesh Gazette, 1 December 2016, Part VI, printed pages 1482–1483 (PDF pages 10–11)
sources.evidence: Schedules explicitly identify mouza Uttar Paragao, thana Dhamrai, district Dhaka. JL values differ between schedules, so none are imported.

sources.title: Dhamrai Upazila official portal: At a glance
sources.evidence: Official upazila portal identifies Dhamrai as an upazila, distinct from the historical thana wording in the Gazette.

sources.title: Kulla Union official portal: At a glance
sources.evidence: Explicit district Dhaka and upazila Dhamrai fields confirm administrative parent relationship.

sources.title: Bangladesh National Portal — district directory
sources.evidence: 64 district names manually checked against the official directory. English names are human transliterations. This does not establish upazila or mouza completeness.

sources.title: Bangladesh National Portal — Dhaka district upazilas
sources.evidence: Dhaka district section explicitly lists Dhamrai, Dohar, Keraniganj, Nawabganj and Savar. Cached page header says 495 nationwide; the newer district portal header says 500. Nationwide completeness is unresolved.

sources.title: Bangladesh National Portal — district-grouped upazila directory snapshot
sources.evidence: Manually transcribed district sections from the cached May 2026 directory (header 495). The newer district directory header says 500; completeness is not established. Duplicate Shaistaganj labels are represented once. Jiyanagar is separately supported by the March 2026 upazila portal renaming notice. English names are human transliterations, not official codes or certified spellings.

sources.title: Jiyanagar Upazila — notice on renaming Indurkani to Jiyanagar
sources.evidence: Official portal indexed notice published 12 March 2026 explicitly names Pirojpur district and renaming Indurkani upazila to Jiyanagar. National directory also lists Jiyanagar. Direct fetch failed; indexed notice text was read, attachment not inspected. No separate Indurkani node or automatic survey identity mapping is created.
